summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -7 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +5.3%; weakest: Sugar #11 -16.4%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.07% (-8 bp in a month), 2-year 4.80% (+3 bp); 2s10s curve +27 bp (-11 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.87 (+2.1% in a month, +5.7% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.921 (+17.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.683 (-0.1%); USD/MXN 19.10 (+3.7%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -6.4% in a month (+5.4% YTD); VIX 27.7. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 83.21 $/bbl (-14.9% in a month), Brent 89.46, ULSD 3.952 $/gal (-16.2%), natural gas 3.26 (-1.1%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -14.7% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.2%, Hang Seng -4.3%, yuan +0.1% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 8 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (24%); S&P GSCI -11.9% in a month; gold -11.2%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
